description: Daily-driver polish for the chat-primary, multi-provider Conan: a context-window meter (T3-5), draft-based new-thread flow (T3-11), reasoning-effort control (T3-6), and @-mention content pinning (T3-3). Every feature must work across claude/codex/grok or degrade honestly via AgentCapabilities - NO provider-name branching in the UI, never render a control a provider can't honour, and never fabricate a number (unknown context window => show counts, no percentage). Source PRD: prd-conan-daily-driver.md. NOTE for the executing agent: read CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md first - Conan is chat-primary; run the gateway with `npm start` (NO watch - restart manually after ANY src/ edit, a stale gateway 404s new routes); verify BOTH :3747 and :5173 after any gateway restart; browser-verify on a throwaway CONAN_PORT/CONAN_UI_PORT stack with CONAN_ALLOWED_ORIGINS set, never on :3747. Subscription auth only - never introduce ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. The paywall is OFF (PAYWALL_ENABLED=false) - no story may add a gate.

userStories.title: Probe + record per-provider context windows and effort mechanisms
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the real context-window sizes and reasoning-effort mechanisms for each provider recorded as verified facts, so the meter and the effort chip are built on truth rather than guesses.
acceptanceCriteria: Record each provider's context-window size per model where it can be VERIFIED (claude 200k / 1M long-context; probe codex and grok). Where a window size cannot be verified, record it explicitly as UNKNOWN - never guess a denominator

Record the verified effort mechanisms already probed: grok `--reasoning-effort` (alias `--effort`) accepts exactly high|medium|low (CLI validates client-side); codex `-c model_reasoning_effort=<level>` is a recognized key (passes `--strict-config`); claude has NO flag - effort is prompt-level phrasing

Record which usage fields each provider reports per turn: claude `input_tokens`+`cache_read_input_tokens`, codex `input_tokens`+`cached_input_tokens`+`output_tokens`, grok `input_tokens`+`cache_read_input_tokens`+`total_tokens`
Write the findings into a doc (e.g. docs/provider-context-effort.md) with an honest UNKNOWN marker wherever a value could not be verified
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Owner: CODEX (no browser verification required). Facts-first story; everything downstream depends on it. Keep probe prompts trivial ('Reply with exactly: ok') and run in a temp dir, never the conan repo. Suggested skills: none.

userStories.title: Report token usage + context position from all three drivers
userStories.description: As a developer, I want every driver to report per-turn token usage and the resulting context-window position, because two of three currently discard the numbers the meter needs.
acceptanceCriteria: ClaudeDriver and GrokDriver populate the existing `tokens` field on the `result` event (today only CodexDriver does; claude/grok emit costUsd and drop usage). Purely ADDITIVE - `costUsd` behaviour is unchanged

Add `contextTokens: number | null` to the `result` event = the latest turn's context-window POSITION (input + cached input), which is distinct from what the turn cost. Null when the provider reports nothing
All three drivers set `contextTokens` from their own usage fields per US-001's table
Parser tests cover the new fields against the existing `src/agent/fixtures/` NDJSON - no live CLI calls in tests
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Owner: CODEX (no browser verification required). Touches all three working drivers - keep it additive so no existing behaviour regresses. Suggested skills: none.

userStories.title: Context-window sizes in the registry + exposed via capabilities
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the window size for the active provider/model available to the UI, so the meter can show a percentage only when the denominator is real.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a context-window lookup to `src/agent/registry.ts` (per provider, per model where it differs), populated from US-001's verified findings

Expose the resolved window size to the client - either on the capabilities frame pushed at session start or on `GET /api/agent/providers`; it must be reachable without the UI branching on a provider name
A provider/model with an UNKNOWN window reports null, never a guessed number
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Owner: CODEX (no browser verification required). Depends on US-001. Keep the table small and data-shaped, like the rest of the registry. Suggested skills: none.

userStories.title: Composer context-window meter
userStories.description: As a user, I want to see how full my context window is (and what the turn cost), so I know when a conversation is near its limit.
acceptanceCriteria: A compact meter in the composer shows the current context position; when the window size is known it also shows a percentage/gauge
When the window size is UNKNOWN, show the raw token count with NO percentage and no gauge - never a fabricated ratio
When the provider reports no usage at all, the meter is absent rather than showing zero
Cost rides alongside where the provider reports it (`capabilities.costUsd`), tokens where it doesn't - reuse the existing per-turn footer logic, no provider-name branching
Updates after each turn; a resumed thread shows the restored position or nothing (never a stale number from another thread)
Renders correctly in light AND dark with semantic tokens only; does not shift the composer layout
Typecheck passes
cd ui && npm run build passes
Verify in browser using automate-browser skill: send turns on claude and on codex, confirm the meter updates and that the unknown-window case degrades to counts
userStories.notes: Owner: CLAUDE (requires browser verification — a port-binding sandbox is needed; do not mark passing without it). First UI story; depends on US-002 + US-003. Browser-verify on a throwaway port stack. Suggested skills: automate-browser, audit-ui.

userStories.title: Local draft threads — no DB row until first send
userStories.description: As a user, I want a new chat to be a local draft so abandoning it doesn't litter my sidebar.
acceptanceCriteria: 'New chat' creates a LOCAL draft only - no `chat_thread` row is written and no sidebar row is persisted until the first message is sent
The draft holds its own launch config (provider, model, permission mode, cwd) so every composer chip works before a thread exists - this is the hidden dependency, not an afterthought
An abandoned draft leaves NOTHING behind: no DB row, no orphaned sidebar entry, nothing after a reload
Existing saved threads still open, resume, and render exactly as before - draft state must not touch the persistence path

Regression coverage in `src/agent/threads.test.ts` (same throwaway-SQLite pattern the file already uses): a thread created through the draft-promotion path persists with its launch config intact (provider, model, cwd), provider stickiness still holds on a conflicting upsert, and `adoptChatThread` still re-keys correctly on resume - these are the invariants a draft refactor can silently break, and nothing else guards them
Be honest about the split: 'no DB row exists before the first send' is UI state and is NOT unit-testable here - it stays a browser check. Do not claim unit coverage for it
Typecheck passes
cd ui && npm run build passes
Verify in browser using automate-browser skill: open a new chat, abandon it, reload, confirm nothing persisted
Tests pass
userStories.notes: VERIFIED ALREADY SATISFIED — no code needed. The story's premise was wrong: `upsertChatThread` is called only from the system event (after the first prompt), and `newThreadIn` only pushes React state. Measured live: chat_thread rows 8 -> 8 across three 'New chat' clicks, and 4 abandoned drafts -> 0 after reload with the DB still at 8. The launch config already lives in ChatPane. The threads.test.ts requirement was predicated on a refactor that proved unnecessary; the promotion invariants are covered by US-006's new idempotence test plus the 7 existing tests. Owner: CLAUDE (requires browser verification — a port-binding sandbox is needed; do not mark passing without it). The riskiest change in this round - it sits on the thread-persistence path, which has real test coverage beneath it (threads.test.ts). Verify resume/reopen explicitly and extend that file rather than trusting the browser alone. Suggested skills: automate-browser.

userStories.title: Draft promotion on first send + one draft per project
userStories.description: As a user, I want my draft to become a real thread the moment I send, and I don't want repeated 'New chat' clicks to pile up empty drafts.
acceptanceCriteria: Sending the first message promotes the draft to a real thread: the row is created with its launch config intact and appears in the sidebar
Clicking 'New chat' while an empty draft already exists for that project REUSES the existing draft instead of creating a second one
The promoted thread behaves identically to one created the old way - resume, reopen, transcript restore, provider avatar
The auto-open-most-recent behaviour (polish US-002) still works and never auto-opens a draft over a real thread

Persistence-level assertion that promotion creates EXACTLY ONE chat_thread row - repeated 'New chat' clicks followed by a single send must not produce duplicates. Assert the row count in `src/agent/threads.test.ts`, not just visually in the browser
Typecheck passes
cd ui && npm run build passes
Verify in browser using automate-browser skill: click New chat twice (one draft), send, confirm promotion + reload persistence
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Owner: CLAUDE (requires browser verification — a port-binding sandbox is needed; do not mark passing without it). Depends on US-005. Suggested skills: automate-browser.

userStories.title: Reasoning-effort descriptor on the capability seam + per-driver application
userStories.description: As a developer, I want reasoning effort expressed as a capability so each provider applies it its own way and the UI never learns provider names.
acceptanceCriteria: Add an effort descriptor to `AgentCapabilities` shaped like `permissionModes` (a list of {id,label,description} in the provider's own vocabulary); an EMPTY list means unsupported

GrokDriver applies `--reasoning-effort <high|medium|low>` (the verified values); CodexDriver applies `-c model_reasoning_effort=<level>`; ClaudeDriver applies a prompt-level prefix since it has no flag - the UI never knows which mechanism is used
The chosen effort rides the launch config and persists per thread
Mirrored UI types stay in sync via the type-only re-export from `src/agent/driver.ts` (do NOT hand-mirror - that drift already shipped once)
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Owner: CODEX (no browser verification required). Depends on US-001's verified mechanisms. Same capability-descriptor pattern as permissionModes. Suggested skills: codebase-design.

userStories.title: Effort chip in the composer (capability-driven)
userStories.description: As a user, I want to ask for more or less thinking, using whatever vocabulary my provider actually supports.
acceptanceCriteria: An effort chip renders beside the existing chips, listing options from the capability descriptor - never a hard-coded list and never a provider-name branch
The chip is ABSENT (not disabled-and-inert) when the provider's effort list is empty
Grok shows high/medium/low; codex shows its levels; claude shows its prompt-level options
Copy must NOT imply the control reveals thinking - reasoning TEXT stays redacted for claude and encrypted for codex (D2)
Renders correctly in light AND dark; locks with the rest of the launch config after the first turn if that matches the existing chip behaviour
Typecheck passes
cd ui && npm run build passes
Verify in browser using automate-browser skill: compare the chip across claude / codex / grok
userStories.notes: Owner: CLAUDE (requires browser verification — a port-binding sandbox is needed; do not mark passing without it). Depends on US-007. Suggested skills: automate-browser.

userStories.title: @-mention pins: attachment model + prompt serialization + size guard
userStories.description: As a user, I want an @-mentioned file's CONTENT sent with my turn, instead of only a path the agent has to re-read.
acceptanceCriteria: A pinned `@` mention becomes a structured attachment on the outgoing turn: the path plus the content actually sent
Pins serialize into the prompt in a clearly delimited block so the agent receives content rather than a path to re-read
A size guard bounds pinned content; anything truncated carries a visible, honest marker - never silent truncation
Pins are per-turn by default (not sticky) unless explicitly kept
Plain (unpinned) `@` path references keep working exactly as today - this is additive
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Owner: CODEX (no browser verification required). Port as REAL context attachments, not prettier chips. File pins only - terminal/element/preview channels are out of scope. Suggested skills: none.

userStories.title: Pin rendering in the composer and transcript
userStories.description: As a user, I want to see exactly what content was pinned and sent, so the transcript never lies about my prompt.

Sent pins render in the transcript attached to their turn, showing what was actually included (and marking truncation where it happened)
A restored/resumed transcript degrades honestly if pin detail isn't recoverable - never imply content was sent that wasn't
Renders correctly in light AND dark with semantic tokens only
